newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - Oct 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - Oct 4.

text.p: These are significant stories or announcements in the Ivorian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy. FRATERNITE MATIN - Ivory Coast's new Moslem spiritual leader, Sheikh Affou Sanogo, 90, tells the government newspaper in an interview he will work to promote national unity and avoid division and intolerance. - Price-cutting airline Air Liberte, placed under a form of administrative observation, suspends flights to Ivory Coast. - Major American companies are showing interest in Ivory Coast, particularly in the oil sector, Ivorian Prime Minister Daniel Kablan Duncan says in an interview - Africa has a right to a second mandate in the post of U.N. Secretary-General and Ivory Coast backs the candidacy of Boutros Boutros-Ghali, Foreign Minister Amara Essy tells U.N. general assembly. LA VOIE - Opposition Ivorian Popular Front leader Laurent Gbagbo denounces government record on curbing criminality - A fourth opposition activist detained during violence surrounding last October's presidential election in Ivory Coast dies in Abidjan's MACA prison. LE JOUR - Ivory Coast Telecommunications Council (CTCI) finally installed as the future regulator of a privatised telecommunications sector. - Government advertisement calls for tenders from Ivory Coast or abroad for the construction and management of a new bus station complex for the commercial capital Abidjan. The complex is to include customer services, administrative offices as well as shops, security, health centre and other facilities. Closing date October 28. - Rene Amany, replaced last month as head of Ivory Coast's Caistab cocoa and coffee marketing board, is named chairman of the board of state-owned Banque Internationale pour l'Afrique Occidentale en Cote d'Ivoire (BIAO-CI), an announcement from the bank says -- Abidjan newsroom +225 21 90 90
